1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The Tonga flag consists of a solid red field, a white canton rectangle in the upper hoist, and a red Greek cross inside the canton. Represent the flag image as an \(m \times n\) matrix \(M\) whose entries are drawn from the two-element set \(\{a,b\}\). Algebraically this matrix admits the decomposition
\[
M = a\cdot\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^\top + (b-a)W,
\]
where the 0-1 matrix \(W\) is the indicator of the white pixels. The white region itself is the difference of three rectangles (the canton minus the horizontal bar of the cross minus the vertical bar of the cross, plus back the overlapping center square). Consequently \(W\) is an integer linear combination of at most four rank-1 indicator matrices, one for each of those rectangles. The all-ones term is itself rank 1, therefore
\[
\rank(M)\le 4.
\]
By choosing the relative dimensions of the rectangles (i.e., the pixel resolution of the image) so that the four indicator vectors are linearly independent, the bound 4 is attained for generic scalars \(a,b\) with \(a\neq b\). Hence the maximal possible rank is exactly 4.

(The same conclusion follows from viewing \(M\) as a block matrix whose blocks are constant on the geometrically distinct rectangular zones of the flag; the number of independent zones is four.)
